question: Sundar lends a sum of ₹6,000 to Mahesh at an interest rate of 10% p.a., compounded annually. What will be the amount at the end of 2 years?
solution:
**Given:- **Principal amount = Rs.6000, time period = 2 years, compounded annually with rate = 10% p.a.

**To find:-** Final amount Mahes has to give,

**Formula used:-** A = P(1+(r)/(n) )ⁿt

Calculation**:- **As it is mentioned that the interest will be compounded yearly,

.·. n = 1 [Means rate would be applied once in a year]

By using the formula of compound interest,

⇒Final amount = P(1+(r)/(1) )¹× t

⇒Final amount = 6000(1+(10)/(100))^ 2

⇒Final amount = 6000((11)/(10))^ 2

⇒Final amount = 6000 × (121)/(100)

⇒Final amount = 60 × 121 = 7260 

**At the end of 2 years, the final amount will be Rs. 7260**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

⇒ __Principle__ → __Amount__

⇒ 10 → 11

⇒ __10 → 11__

⇒ Total → 100 → 121

∴ If Principle = 100x, then Amount = 121x

⇒ 100x = 6000

⇒ x = 60 

**∴ Amount = 121x = 121 × 60 = Rs. 7260.**
